additionalEvidence.title: Saltaire · export contracts disrupted by war
additionalEvidence.summary: At the outbreak of war, Germany and Russia cancelled outstanding yarn contracts with Salts Mill. The collection reports that these two markets together had accounted for 90% of exported yarn; the mill moved to short-time working.

source.title: Saltaire Collection — World connections
source.locator: 1910s: James Roberts’ interests in Russia; paragraph on cancelled contracts at outbreak of war in 1914

additionalEvidence.timeCaveat: 1914 wartime-disruption episode, not a full-year export-flow observation. Later Russian exports resumed, but the source provides no precise resumption date.
additionalEvidence.spatialCaveat: UNESCO Saltaire property representative point; no factory footprint or shipping route implied.
additionalEvidence.referenceCountryCaveat: Modern national reference lookup only, not factory sales or historical sovereignty.
additionalEvidence.reviewStatus: Collection exhibition inspected; underlying Roberts letter-book not independently audited.

reuse.status: Original concise paraphrase with attribution; blanket source reproduction licence not established.
